arxiv-2110-02464.title: Anomalously small superconducting gap in the strong spin-orbit coupled superconductor: β − \beta- Tungsten
arxiv-2110-02464.creator: Prashant Chauhan, Ramesh Budhani, N. P. Armitage
arxiv-2110-02464.description: Abstract Thin films of β − \beta- tungsten host superconductivity in the presence of strong spin-orbit coupling. This non-equilibrium crystalline phase of tungsten has attracted considerable attention in recent years due to its giant spin Hall effect and the potential promise of exotic superconductivity.

arxiv-2201-09240.title: Learning-Driven Lossy Image Compression; A Comprehensive Survey
arxiv-2201-09240.creator: Sonain Jamil, Md. Jalil Piran, and MuhibUr Rahman
arxiv-2201-09240.description: Abstract In the realm of image processing and computer vision (CV), machine learning (ML) architectures are widely applied. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) solve a wide range of image processing issues and can solve image compression problem. Compression of images is necessary due to bandwidth and memory constraints.

arxiv-2406-06882.title: A Characterization for Tightness of the Sparse Moment-SOS Hierarchy
arxiv-2406-06882.creator: Jiawang Nie, Zheng Qu, Xindong Tang, Linghao Zhang
arxiv-2406-06882.description: Abstract . This paper studies the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy of relaxations for solving sparse polynomial optimization problems. We show that this sparse hierarchy is tight if and only if the objective can be written as a sum of sparse nonnegative polynomials, each of which belongs to the sum of the ideal and quadratic module generated by the corresponding sparse constraints.

arxiv-2410-19133.title: Hybrid Preferences: Learning to Route Instances for Human vs. AI Feedback
arxiv-2410-19133.creator: Lester James V. Miranda, Yizhong Wang, Yanai Elazar, Sachin Kumar, Valentina Pyatkin, Faeze Brahman, Noah A. Smith, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Pradeep Dasigi
arxiv-2410-19133.description: Abstract Learning from human feedback has enabled the alignment of language models (LMs) with human preferences. However, collecting human preferences is expensive and time-consuming, with highly variable annotation quality. An appealing alternative is to distill preferences from LMs as a source of synthetic annotations, offering a cost-effective and scalable alternative, albeit susceptible to other biases and errors.

arxiv-2506-00900.title: SocialEval : Evaluating Social Intelligence of Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-00900.creator: Jinfeng Zhou, Yuxuan Chen, Yihan Shi, Xuanming Zhang, Leqi Lei, Yi Feng Zexuan Xiong Miao Yan Xunzhi Wang Yaru Cao Jianing Yin, Shuai Wang Quanyu Dai Zhenhua Dong Hongning Wang Minlie Huang
arxiv-2506-00900.description: Abstract LLMs exhibit promising Social Intelligence (SI) in modeling human behavior, raising the need to evaluate LLMs’ SI and their discrepancy with humans. SI equips humans with interpersonal abilities to behave wisely in navigating social interactions to achieve social goals.

arxiv-2507-10478.title: Predicting the Acoustic Signatures of Saturn’s Upper Atmosphere
arxiv-2507-10478.creator: Andrew Powell, Andi Petculescu, Rishabh Chaudhary, Robert White, Don Banfield, Ian Neeson, [1em] University of Louisiana at Lafayette (Lafayette, LA)
arxiv-2507-10478.description: Abstract Predictions for the acoustic attenuation coefficient and phase speed as functions of frequency and altitude in Saturn’s atmosphere are presented and discussed. The pressure range considered in the study is 1 mbar to 1 bar, in windless and cloudless conditions.

arxiv-2511-04706.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) distinguish themselves by quickly delivering information and providing personalized responses through natural language prompts. However, they also infer user demographics, which can raise ethical concerns about bias and implicit personalization and create an echo chamber effect.

arxiv-2601-03729.title: MATANet: A Multi-context Attention and Taxonomy-Aware Network for Fine-Grained Underwater Recognition of Marine Species
arxiv-2601-03729.creator: Donghwan Lee, Byeongjin Kim, Geunhee Kim, Hyukjin Kwon, Nahyeon Maeng, Wooju Kim
arxiv-2601-03729.description: Abstract Fine-grained classification of marine animals supports ecology, biodiversity and habitat conservation, and evidence-based policy-making. However, existing methods often overlook contextual interactions from the surrounding environment and insufficiently incorporate the hierarchical structure of marine biological taxonomy. To address these challenges, we propose MATANet (Multi-context Attention and Taxonomy-Aware Network), a novel model designed for fine-grained marine species classification.

pmc-10526337.creator: Jeong Wook Kang, Hyeon-Kyoung Cheong, Su Il Kim, Min Kyeong Lee, Young Chan Lee, In-Hwan Oh, Young-Gyu Eun, Han-Fei Ding
pmc-10526337.description: Simple SummaryThe incidence of hypopharyngeal cancer has been rapidly increasing, but hypopharyngeal cancer has a poorer prognosis compared to other head and neck cancers. This is because the diagnosis of hypopharyngeal cancer is late due to few symptoms in the early stages. Thus, early diagnosis and prevention are very important in the management of hypopharyngeal cancer.

pmc-10627645.title: Feasibility of 125I brachytherapy combined with arterial infusion chemotherapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer
pmc-10627645.creator: Shujing Huang, Yanqing Cao, Rui Wang, Huimin Liu, Ting Wang, Shu Yang
pmc-10627645.description: To evaluation the feasibility of Iodine-125 (¹²5I) brachytherapy combined with arterial infusion chemotherapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer. A total of 72 cases with Stage III and IV were retrospectively reviewed. 23 cases receiving 125I brachytherapy were classified as Group A.

pmc-10671664.title: Improved 2,3-Butanediol Production Rate of Metabolically Engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae by Deletion of RIM15 and Activation of Pyruvate Consumption Pathway
pmc-10671664.creator: Masahiko Sugimura, Taisuke Seike, Nobuyuki Okahashi, Yoshihiro Izumi, Takeshi Bamba, Jun Ishii, Fumio Matsuda, Danilo Porro
pmc-10671664.description: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a promising host for the bioproduction of higher alcohols, such as 2,3-butanediol (2,3-BDO). Metabolically engineered S. cerevisiae strains that produce 2,3-BDO via glycolysis have been constructed. However, the specific 2,3-BDO production rates of engineered strains must be improved.

pmc-12387879.title: Multimodal Assessment of Ocular Parameters in Patients with Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea with Emphasis on Retinal Structural Changes
pmc-12387879.creator: Anita Pusic Sesar, Anja Cehajic, Antonela Geber, Mia Zoric Geber, Ivan Cavar, Antonio Sesar, Wen-Dien Chang, Yung-An Tsou
pmc-12387879.description: Background: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is increasingly recognized as a potential risk factor for glaucoma due to its association with intermittent hypoxia and vascular dysregulation. The aim of this study was to investigate early glaucomatous changes in the eyes of patients with OSA. Methods: This case–control study included 25 patients with OSA and 25 age- and sex-matched healthy controls.

pmc-12418377.title: Extremophile hotspots linked to containerized industrial waste dumping in a deep-sea basin
pmc-12418377.creator: Johanna Gutleben, Sheila Podell, Kira Mizell, Douglas Sweeney, Carlos Neira, Lisa A Levin, Paul R Jensen, Christopher Dupont
pmc-12418377.description: Decaying barrels on the seafloor linked to DDT contamination have raised concerns about the public health implications of decades old industrial waste dumped off the coast of Los Angeles. To explore their contents, we collected sediment cores perpendicular to five deep-sea barrels.

pmc-12630801.title: BIGH3 is a mediator of TGFβ-Induced collagen formation in fibrosis and pancreatic cancer and a potential therapeutic target
pmc-12630801.creator: Nicholas Willumsen, Kim Henriksen, Cecilie Bager, Anette T. Hansen Selnø, Khaled E. Mohamed, Diana J. Leeming, Mark Alexander Skarsfeldt, Neel I. Nissen, Rasmus S. Pedersen, Jeppe Thorlacius-Ussing, Morten H. Dziegiel, Man-Hung Eric Tang, Lars N. Jørgensen, Hadi M. H. Diab, Inna M. Chen, Julia S. Jo
pmc-12630801.description: Fibroblast-driven deposition of extracellular matrix, particularly type III collagen, is linked to poor outcomes in patients with liver fibrosis, fibrotic solid tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma and pancreatic cancer as well as in patients with other fibrotic diseases. The pro-peptide of type III collagen (PRO-C3) serves as a serum biomarker of active collagen formation.

pmc-12744140.title: Retrospective Review of Fluoroscopy Exposure Comparing Open vs MIS Bunionectomy Procedures
pmc-12744140.creator: Heba Ahmad, Michael Greaser, William McGarvey, Taggart Gauvain
pmc-12744140.description: Research Type:Level 3 - Retrospective cohort study, Case-control study, Meta-analysis of Level 3 studiesIntroduction/Purpose:Hallux valgus is a common forefoot pathology. Minimally Invasive Chevron-Akin (MICA) procedure is a common surgical technique that has been shown to reduce post operative complications, preserve soft tissues, and improve recovery. Minimally invasive techniques are gaining popularity in orthopedics.

pmc-12779427.title: Quantity-effect correlation between water intake and serum uric acid in US adults: a cross-sectional study based on NHANES data
pmc-12779427.creator: Xiang-Liang Meng, Chao Zhang, Tao Liu, Zhao-Kun Shi, Yi-Xin Zhang, Wei Hu, Ling-Di Chang, Jun Ding, Xiao-Long Cao, Li Guo, Ke-Ying Zhang, Wei-Jun Qin
pmc-12779427.description: BackgroundHyperuricemia (HUA) imposes a substantial clinical and public health burden, affecting 43 million adults in the U.S. and 170 million in China. Increased hydration is often recommended as a preventive measure for HUA, but the quantity-effect correlation between water intake and serum uric acid (SUA) is unclear. This study aimed to investigate the quantity-effect correlation between water intake and SUA.

pmc-13210749.title: Real-Time Edge-Prior Guided SegFormer for Robust Contour Extraction of Aggregate Particles in Conveyor-Belt Depth Maps
pmc-13210749.creator: Jian Shen, Hanye Liu, Zhilin Chen, Xiangnan Zhao, Huijuan Yang
pmc-13210749.description: Accurate contour extraction of aggregate particles from conveyor-belt depth maps is essential for downstream particle counting and size measurement, yet industrial depth data often contains weak discontinuities, missing values, and speckle-like noise. We propose a task-specific geometry-aware contour extraction framework that combines a compact SegFormer encoder with depth-derived priors, a lightweight local branch, edge-prior gated fusion, and full-resolution residual refinement.

pmc-13218675.title: Thyroid hormone acts independently of the thyroid hormone receptor beta in hepatocytes to improve systemic insulin sensitivity
pmc-13218675.creator: Anne H. van der Spek, Megan J. Ritter, Izuki Amano, Lorraine Soares de Oliveira, Joseph E. Kaserman, Isabella Salguero Cespedes, Taylor Vierling, Andrew A. Wilson, Anthony N. Hollenberg
pmc-13218675.description: Background:Insulin resistance plays a key role in the development of type 2 diabetes and predates the development of frank hyperglycemia. Thyroid hormone (TH) signaling plays a critical role in glucose homeostasis, as both hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism have been linked to the development of insulin resistance and diabetes.

pmc-13237027.title: Circulating pro-angiogenic cells are preserved despite myocardial angiogenic signal deficits in HFpEF model
pmc-13237027.creator: Pallavi Shrivastava, Rukayat A. Raji, Abdallah Jwayyed, Huijing Xia, Marian E. Okon, Ifechukwude J. Biose
pmc-13237027.description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has no cure, and microvascular dysfunction is a major contributing factor to its pathophysiology. Circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) and Angiogenic T (i.e., Tang) cells which support vascular repair are deficient in clinical HFpEF.

pmc-13711442.title: Stroke After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With Contemporary Valves: Insights From the OCEAN-TAVI Registry
pmc-13711442.creator: Yusuke Watanabe, Masanori Yamamoto, Hirofumi Hioki, Masafumi Saito, Jo Omiya, Kento Kito, Yasuyuki Tsuchida, Yosei Iseki, Masataka Arakawa, Mizuki Miura, Akihisa Kataoka, Takahiro Tokuda, Shinichi Shirai, Kenichi Ishizu, Toru Naganuma, Futoshi Yamanaka, Masahiko Noguchi, Yohei Ohno, Tetsuro Shimura,
pmc-13711442.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundStroke remains a serious complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), even with contemporary devices. The objective of the study was to evaluate the incidence, predictors, and prognosis of in-hospital stroke in patients undergoing TAVR with contemporary valve platforms.MethodsWe analyzed 5123 patients from the multicenter OCEAN-TAVI registry who underwent TAVR with SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA, Evolut FX, or Navitor between May 2022 and December 2024. Stroke incidence across valve types was compared using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW).
